question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer must mirror the traffic on a switch. The engineer locates the server port that requires monitoring on switch1, but the packet sniffer is on switch2. The engineer must configure the source IP address on switch1. Which command accomplishes this goal?
context:
switch1#show run interface Vlan 10
interface Vlan10
  description Service Datacenter-Rack-A
  ip address 209.165.200.225 255.255.255.224
!
end
switch1#
theory: ERSPAN encapsulates mirrored traffic in a GRE tunnel sourced from the switch's own IP address and destined to the collector's IP; when the switch doesn't have an interface whose address naturally matches what should appear as that tunnel's source, the global monitor erspan origin ip-address command explicitly sets which local IP the switch uses as the GRE/ERSPAN source for all its ERSPAN sessions. This differs from per-session commands like source interface, which selects the mirrored traffic itself rather than the encapsulation's source address, which is why an explicit origin IP command is required here. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — ERSPAN Origin IP Address Configuration)
